transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Maya (CTO), Ethan (Lead ML Engineer), Priya (PM), Zoe (Infra)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on Redwood PLG / quickstart for Hosted API, questions about time-to-first-token, free credits, and later path to Dedicated/Private for production. Security questions (SOC2, SSO, KMS) and initial perf targets discussed. Agreed next steps to send quickstart + credits and run a small benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Maya: yep, loud and clear, thanks for doing this.
[00:05] Ava: awesome. quick intros — im ava, account exec, and liam is our se who'll handle the technical deepdive.
[00:12] Liam: hi all, thanks - excited to learn about your use case.
[00:15] Priya: im priya, product, i'll be owning the evaluation from our side.
[00:18] Ethan: ethan, lead ml eng, i'll be doing the integration.
[00:21] Zoe: zoe, infra, i'll ask about networking and security.
[00:24] Ava: great. quick agenda: 1) understand current stack and goals, 2) show quickstart/self-serve flow and credits, 3) discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private for your scale, 4) next steps. sound good?
[00:31] Maya: yep perfect. our short background - silverwave builds analytics pipelines for maritime traffic, we run a mix of batch and near-real-time features. we're prototyping generative features for anomaly summaries and operational alerts.
[00:44] Ethan: big constraints are latency (we want sub-200 ms p50 token generation ideally for alerts) and cost - we also have regulatory constraints for certain customers that may require data residency.
[00:56] Ava: got it. what's your current infra? cloud? k8s?
[00:59] Zoe: aws, k8s clusters, internal VPCs. we use SSO (Okta) and have a KMS for keys.
[01:06] Ava: perfect, that's a common setup. quick question on expected QPS for the pilot?
[01:10] Priya: for pilot maybe 50 rps average, spikes to 200 for short windows.
[01:15] Liam: ok good to know. so for PLG/self-serve the fastest path is Redwood Hosted API — you sign up, get free credits, call tokens, you can be at first token in minutes. our SDKs have examples for node/python.
[01:27] Ethan: how quick is first-token? do you have an onboarding guide?
[01:30] Liam: yes, usually under 10 minutes for devs: sign up, create API key, run quickstart script. we'll send the quickstart doc after the call. free dev credits are applied to new accounts automatically if you're part of the trial program.
[01:41] Maya: and if we need guaranteed throughput or lower latency, what's the path? Dedicated?
[01:45] Ava: correct - Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity for predictable throughput and isolation. it's a contract/commit model. Private (VPC/on-prem) is full control for highly regulated workloads. many customers start with Hosted to iterate then move to Dedicated when they need predictability.
[01:59] Ethan: we might need dedicated for customer contracts. curious on the quantization/latency tradeoffs — do you support quantized models in hosted?
[02:08] Liam: hosted supports a curated catalog—some variants are quantized; we also surface per-model performance profiles. the runtime picks kernels, does batching, kv cache, etc. quantization helps cost, sometimes at slight quality delta, we can recommend profiles based on your prompts.
[02:22] Zoe: on networking — for hosted, traffic goes over public endpoints, we can use private networking to Dedicated?
[02:28] Ava: yes for Dedicated you can have VPC peering and private endpoints. Private deployments can be fully inside your VPC or on-prem.
[02:35] Priya: security docs — can you share SOC2 and audit logs info?
[02:38] Ava: yes we'll share the security pack and SOC2 report. we also support SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS integrations for Private.
[02:48] Maya: do you support bring-your-own-model or only Redwood-curated models?
[02:52] Liam: Hosted has a model catalog with curated open models; Dedicated/Private give more flexibility to bring your own model artifacts or pin to specific versions. we can onboard custom models with a short onboarding process.
[03:02] Ethan: great. about pricing — we want to estimate unit cost for token generation at 512 tokens per request, 50 rps. can you help ballpark?
[03:11] Ava: we'll ask liam to run a rough estimate from our perf numbers; we'll send a spreadsheet showing cost with and without batching and with quantized variants.
[03:19] Liam: yes i'll prepare a table — assuming X ms p50 on hosted for the model family, and dedicated pricing if you go to reserved capacity, i'll show delta.
[03:27] Priya: for the pilot we only need hosted to iterate. presumably we can add rate limits and quotas?
[03:31] Ava: yes, you can configure quotas and keys per team. Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns.
[03:38] Zoe: any compliance concerns for EU customers? data residency?
[03:42] Ava: we have regions across NA and EU; for strict residency we recommend Private deployments or Dedicated in an EU region.
[03:49] Maya: ok good. what's the typical timeline to go from Hosted pilot to Dedicated?
[03:53] Ava: that varies but operationally customers go to Dedicated in 4-8 weeks after the pilot if the traffic pattern is stable and ROI is clear. provisioning and configs can be accelerated if you have a contract in place.
[04:04] Ethan: curious about evaluation benchmarks — can you run a small benchmark for our payloads?
[04:08] Liam: yes — easiest path: you share a sample of anonymized prompts and expected sequence lengths, we run a pilot benchmark on Hosted and optionally on Dedicated config (we can simulate). we'll provide latency and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:20] Ethan: i'll prepare that. what's the preferred format?
[04:22] Liam: JSON lines with prompt + expected reply length is great. we'll put a template in the quickstart doc.
[04:28] Priya: any redflags — we heard from other vendors about cold-start latencies in hosted envs. how does Redwood handle idle models?
[04:36] Liam: runtime uses smart routing and KV caching, warm pools; for very low-latency SLOs we recommend Dedicated pinned capacity to avoid cold starts. Hosted does warm-up heuristics but not the same guarantee.
[04:47] Maya: ok. also, do you provide SDK examples for canary rollouts or A/B testing?
[04:51] Ava: yes, Console supports rollouts, canary policies, auto-fallback to cheaper model variants. we'll share docs and a sample canary config.
[05:00] Zoe: about keys and KMS — for hosted are keys managed by you, or can we bring our own?
[05:05] Liam: for Hosted the API keys are managed; for Private you can bring KMS/HSM and manage keys. Dedicated has KMS integration options too.
[05:13] Priya: what's the best next step to get us to first-token and try the quickstart?
[05:16] Ava: i'll email the quickstart + free credits instructions after the call, include SDK snippets and the benchmark template. sign-up should get you credits and you can be calling in under 10 minutes.
[05:26] Maya: sounds good. real quick — can we get SOC2 docs before we start? procurement wants it for pilot approval.
[05:31] Ava: yes we'll attach the security pack in that email.
[05:34] Ethan: ok i'll also invite the infra team to the shared drive and upload the sample prompts.
[05:38] Priya: timeline: aim to have pilot up next week and benchmark the following.
[05:42] Ava: perfect. to recap: we'll send quickstart + credits + security pack, liam will run rough latency/cost estimate after they share prompts, customer will upload sample dataset, then we schedule a short benchmark session.
[05:55] Maya: thanks so much.
[05:57] Ava: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email.

End of call.
